validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed by FIVE independent, verified, non-GEM sources naming this exact line: (1) Kazakhstan Today (kt.kz, 2015-02-02), quoting a KazTransGas press release on a pipe-rupture/fire at km 288, which names the operator as 'UMG Uralsk, AO Intergaz Tsentralnaya Aziya (a subsidiary of AO KazTransGaz)'; (2) Neftegas.info (2023-04-20), reporting Gazprom Transgaz Yekaterinburg's completion of >95km of pipe repairs on 'MG Orenburg-Novopskov'; (3) CDU TEK (cdu.ru, Russian federal fuel-energy dispatch office, article referencing 2021 KMG data), which lists 'Orenburg-Novopskov' among the named trunk lines carrying Russian gas through Kazakhstan; (4) Intergas Central Asia's own official 'General Information' page (intergas.kz), which lists MG 'Orenburg-Novopskov' as one of the trunk pipelines operated by its Uralsk UMG branch; (5) Kapital.kz (2021-02-23), quoting Russia's Energy Ministry on a Feb-2021 pressure-drop/supply interruption on 'MG Orenburg-Novopskov (OOO Gazpromtransgaz Yekaterinburg)' that briefly halted transit to Kazakhstan via GIS Alekseyevka. CLASSIFICATION: transmission/trunk (магистральный газопровод) is correct -- every source above describes it in exactly those terms. GEM's own CountriesOrAreas field already correctly reads 'Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Russia' (NumberOfCountries=3), i.e. GEM does NOT mis-tag this as a purely-Kazakhstan pipeline -- it is modeled (correctly) as one multi-country system, consistent with how the CAC family (P2291/P5770/P5771) is handled. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of P0761 (Soyuz) -- Intergas Central Asia's own Q2-2021 internal capacity register (see spec finding below) lists 'Союз' (1400mm, 423km KZ) and 'Оренбург-Новопсков' (1200/1220mm, 382km KZ) as two SEPARATE numbered rows under the same Uralsk UMG branch, and GEM's own P0761 (2750km, 1420mm, ends Uzhgorod) vs P0791 (1230km, 1220mm, ends Novopskov) already have non-overlapping length/diameter/endpoint. Also checked the wider 'Novopskov hub' family already in the GEM sheet (P0789 Urengoy-Novopskov, P0790 Petrovsk-Novopskov, P1471 Novopskov-Aksai-Mozdok, P1483 Novopskov-Shebelinka) -- Novopskov is evidently a major compressor/convergence node where several distinct Soviet-era trunk lines terminate; P0791 (Orenburg origin) is cleanly distinct from its Urengoy- and Petrovsk-origin siblings, not a relabeled duplicate of any of them. PipelineNetworkGrouping check (per task instructions, comparing to P0761's wrong 'Brotherhood pipeline system' tag): P0791's PipelineNetworkGrouping and PipelineNetworkGroupingAlt are both BLANK in the live sheet -- it does NOT carry P0761's defect (there is nothing wrong to fix here, and I found no source giving an authoritative network-grouping label to force a fill).

validity.researcher_notes: Per the task's specific instruction to establish what portion (if any) is in Kazakhstan and whether the 1,230km length is Kazakh-scoped or whole-system: it is WHOLE-SYSTEM, not Kazakh-scoped, and this is well supported. The Kazakh section ALONE is officially 382 km -- stated verbatim by KazTransGas's own press release, independently reported by Kazakhstan Today (kt.kz, 2015): 'Казахстанский участок газопровода Оренбург - Новопсков был введен в эксплуатацию в 1975 году. Протяженность МГ Оренбург - Новопсков - 382 километра, диаметр - 1220 миллиметров, проектное давление - до 5,4 МПа.' This 382km figure is independently cross-validated by Intergas Central Asia's own Q2-2021 internal capacity register (a primary operator document, row 7: 'Оренбург-Новопсков, 1200mm, 382km') and by summing the same register's Soyuz (423km) + Orenburg-Novopskov (382km) = 805km, which is an EXACT match to KMG's Annual Report 2021 combined figure for 'Soyuz, Orenburg-Novopskov' (805km/40.4 bcm/y) -- strong internal consistency across the KMG/Intergas corporate family (note: KMG and Intergas are affiliated, parent-subsidiary, so this pairing is one corporate origin, not two independent ones, but the arithmetic cross-check is still meaningful). Given the Kazakh segment is only 382km, GEM's LengthKnown=1230.00km must represent the WHOLE international line (Orenburg, Russia -> transiting Kazakhstan near Uralsk -> back into Russia -> Novopskov, Luhansk Oblast, Ukraine). This is corroborated two ways: (a) Ukrainian Wikipedia's dedicated article on this pipeline (tertiary, but detailed and internally coherent) states total length 1,356km 'per Gazprom data', diameter 1220mm, commissioned 1975, with 382km specifically 'passing through the territory of Kazakhstan' -- consistent in every particular except the whole-system total, which is ~10% higher than GEM's 1230km (I could not independently verify the 1356km figure against a primary Gazprom document, so I am not proposing it as a correction, only noting the gap); (b) far more compellingly, I pulled the pipeline's OWN routes-repo GeoJSON (data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P0791.geojson, a 62-point LineString) and computed its great-circle length: ~1,219km, essentially identical to GEM's own LengthEstimateKm=1222.71 and within 1% of LengthKnown=1230.00. The drawn route starts at Orenburg's coordinates (55.11E, 51.78N), threads through the Uralsk, Kazakhstan area (~51.1-51.5E, 51.3N, exactly where the 382km Kazakh segment sits) for roughly 4 of its 62 vertices, then re-enters Russia and ends EXACTLY at Novopskov's coordinates (39.15E, 49.52N). This is strong, self-consistent evidence that GEM's declared 1230km is a genuine whole-system measurement, not an accidental Kazakh-only or mis-scoped value -- and that the route geometry (which actually crosses into Kazakhstan) supports the multi-country CountriesOrAreas tag. Net: no correction recommended; flagging as a documented caveat only, since neither GEM nor I can pin the whole-system total to an external primary source at two-decimal precision (1230 vs the unconfirmed 1356 Wikipedia/Gazprom figure).

Exact match, two independent sources. Kazakhstan Today quotes KazTransGas's own press release verbatim: 'Казахстанский участок газопровода Оренбург - Новопсков был введен в эксплуатацию в 1975 году' (the Kazakh section was commissioned in 1975). CDU TEK (Russian federal fuel-energy dispatch office) states, per-line (not a system aggregate): 'Оренбург - Новопсков (российский природный газ; 14,6 млрд куб. м в год)' -- an EXACT match to GEM's 14.60 bcm/y. Kept at tier=medium rather than high because I have only one source stating this exact per-line figure explicitly; however it cross-validates well against Intergas Central Asia's own Q2-2021 internal capacity register, which gives a COMBINED Soyuz+Orenburg-Novopskov actual-capacity figure of 40,820 million m3/year (40.82 bcm/y) -- and the same cdu.ru source separately states Soyuz alone = 25.2 bcm/y, so 25.2+14.6=39.8 bcm/y, closely matching the Intergas combined total (design vs actual-utilization variance is expected). This is the same 'system total vs per-line' pattern flagged on the CAC family (P2291 etc.), but here it resolves IN GEM'S FAVOR -- 14.6 is a genuine per-line figure, not a system total misapplied to a single string.
